transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Emma Ortiz (Calypso Head ML Ops), Liam Byrne (Platform), Sofia Martinez (Security), Noah Kim (Product)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be fuzzy):
Calypso is evaluating a POC to validate Redwood for production inference for a mix of long-form document summarization and short classification calls. Primary focus: workload characterization (QPS, concurrency), input/output token distributions, and pass/fail benchmarks for latency, correctness regressions, and cost. Security must meet SOC2 like controls, KMS for keys, and EU data residency for parts of the workload. Next steps: Redwood to run pilot benchmarks, share pricing and security docs, schedule SOC2 deep-dive.

Topics: workload sizing, QPS targets, concurrency model, token length distributions, batching/kv cache, dedicated vs hosted, timelines.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, i'm maya, ae on the payments vertical, ravi is our se, he'll run the bench and help with architecture.
[00:18] Emma (Calypso): Thanks maya. i'll kick off - we run two main inference patterns: long-form summarization of customer dispute docs (~5-10k tokens input, output ~500-1k tokens) and short classification for transaction-tagging (~20-150 input tokens, output ~10-20). Most traffic is daytime real-time qa for agents.
[00:38] Liam: To add, we have about 300 agents concurrently during peak and expect bot workflow to produce ~4-6 qps sustained and peaks up to 40 qps across global regions. but crucially concurrency per customer session tends to be low, like 1-2 concurrent calls per agent.
[00:58] Ravi (Redwood SE): Okay that's super helpful. when you say peaks up to 40 qps is that aggregate across all regions or per region?
[01:05] Emma: Aggregate, north america is ~70% of traffic. eu is 20, rest asia 10.
[01:12] Noah (Product): success criteria: p95 latency for short calls under 200ms, for long summarization under 3s for a 1k output target. Also minimal accuracy/regression vs our current baseline LLM - cannot be more than 2% drop on our key NLU metrics.
[01:36] Maya: Great, those are clear. on hosting, are you leaning towards Redwood Dedicated or Private?
[01:44] Sofia (Security): We're leaning Private for PCI scope reasons, but open to Dedicated if we can get VPC peering, KMS integration, and audit logs turned on. also data residency - some customer docs must remain in eu.
[02:01] Ravi: Understood. for a POC we often run a hybrid: benchmark on Dedicated (predictable latency) and then evaluate Private deployment for data residency. we can mirror traffic to eu region and show latency/cost tradeoffs.
[02:18] Emma: ok, what do you need from us to size the workload?
[02:22] Ravi: we'll need: token distribution histogram (we can approximate if you don't have exact), expected qps distribution (sustained vs peak), payload concurrency expectations, and a small labeled eval set for quality checks. also, any rate limiting patterns or burst windows you expect.
[02:40] Emma: we have logs. i'll pull token length percentiles - rough numbers now: 60% short calls <200 tokens, 25% medium 200-1k tokens, 15% long >1k tokens (rare 5-10k). avg output tokens: short 15, medium 80, long 700.
[03:00] Liam: and our SLA requirement is 99.9 for availability during business hours, p95 latency as mentioned.
[03:09] Maya: good. Ravi, on the modeling side, what QPS mix will you simulate?
[03:14] Ravi: we'll create a QPS mixer: baseline 5 qps sustained with simulated peaks to 40 qps for 2-5 minute bursts, concurrency targets 8-12 concurrent generator threads for the region. we'll also include a KV cache/prefix cache scenario for the long docs to emulate re-use. note: transcription may say K V cash, we mean KV cache.
[03:39] Emma: how much capacity should we reserve for bench? we're trying to understand cost tradeoffs - dedicated nodes vs hosted ephemeral.
[03:45] Ravi: for initial bench: run on a single 4-GPU dedicated-style node (we'll match it to Redwood Dedicated profile) and also run a smaller Private instance for eu region. the bench will include 10k synthetic requests with the distribution you provided plus 2k real example traces. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per million tokens.
[04:08] Noah: can you estimate expected tokens/sec for the mix?
[04:11] Ravi: rough back-of-envelope: with 5 qps baseline and avg input+output tokens about 200 for the mix, that's ~1k tokens/sec aggregate. at peak 40 qps with more long calls it could hit 6-8k tokens/sec. exacts depend on batching and kv cache hit rate.
[04:28] Sofia: what about cold start for long context? we worry about KV cache priming and the effect on latency for first request.
[04:34] Ravi: yes first-request latency will be higher; with Redwood's continuous batching and KV cache we expect amortized cost to be lower. for POC we'll include measurements for cache cold vs warm: priming with a small dataset then measuring delta.
[04:48] Emma: security: can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs export?
[04:54] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit log exports. Dedicated can be configured with VPC peering and log forwarding; we'll include detailed docs.
[05:05] Sofia: and SOC2 type II?
[05:08] Maya: Redwood is SOC2 and ISO certified; we'll share certificates.
[05:12] Liam: timeline - we need a 6 week pilot ideally to present to the board. what's realistic?
[05:19] Ravi: candidly, 6 weeks is doable: week 1 onboarding + infra setup, week 2 bench runs, week 3 integration with a sample agent workflow, week 4 evaluation and quality checks, week 5 iterate on tuning (quantization/batching), week 6 final reporting and decision.
[05:35] Emma: ok good. on the quality metric you mentioned 2% regression cap, how do we define that?
[05:40] Noah: we'll use our labeled test set of ~1k examples across intents. pass if F1 drop <2% compared to baseline.
[05:48] Ravi: for benchmarks we'll produce a single report with latency, throughput, cost, and quality delta. also include recommended batch sizes and quantization profile.
[05:58] Maya: are there any other constraints - egress costs, certificate rotation, or compliance hoops?
[06:03] Sofia: we need key rotation policy and proof of data residency control for eu. also a signed DPA.
[06:10] Maya: will do.
[06:12] Emma: quick question about caching - a lot of our queries are repeated templates; does Redwood support prefix caching or token-level caching?
[06:19] Ravi: yes, runtime has prefix/KV caching; it can dedupe and reuse KV cache across requests if you keep session keys. we'll simulate different cache hit rates - 0%, 30%, 60% - to show impact on latency and cost.
[06:33] Liam: any plan for concurrent model variants or fallbacks in the POC? we sometimes want a cheaper distill variant for non-sensitive calls.
[06:40] Maya: that's part of our Optimize toolkit - we can recommend model variants and automatic fallback policies by route. we'll include that in the playbook.
[06:48] Noah: pricing question - ballpark on cost per 1M tokens for dedicated vs hosted?
[06:52] Maya: we'll include a tailored pilot pricing with committed reserved capacity and an on-demand comparison; i'll send a detailed spreadsheet.
[06:58] Emma: ok, to summarize next steps?
[07:02] Maya: sure - recap: maya sends pricing and SOW; ravi will run initial bench (10k synthetic + 2k real traces) and share results; sofia will get security checklist to redwood and schedule SOC2 deep-dive; schedule follow up for 2026-12-20 to review bench.
[07:19] Emma: sounds good. thanks all.
[07:22] End of recorded transcript (note: timestamps in transcript are approximate and there may be mis-attributed speaker labels or minor transcription errors).
